scenarios.prompt: Create a Codex skill for reviewing SQL migrations. It should activate for migration reviews, avoid general SQL questions, and include only resources that materially help.

assertions.description: Produces a valid skill directory whose folder and frontmatter name match and whose description has a precise trigger boundary.
Adds only resources with a concrete role and leaves no unfinished scaffold content.

scenarios.prompt: We need three related Codex skills that each turn a different compliance checklist into a reviewed Markdown report. Design a reusable starting blueprint and scaffold the first skill.

assertions.description: Selects and justifies a blueprint whose resources match the repeated workflow.
Identifies required customization points and produces a scaffold that remains release-blocking until placeholders are resolved.

scenarios.prompt: Update this existing Codex skill's authoring instructions, but preserve its explicit-only invocation policy, MCP dependencies, icons, and unrelated scripts.

assertions.description: Inspects existing files first and preserves unrelated policy, dependencies, assets, and scripts.
Makes only the requested authoring change and validates the updated skill.

scenarios.prompt: Audit this Codex skill for routing, portability, and unsafe filesystem behavior. Give evidence-linked findings, but do not modify anything.

assertions.description: Performs read-only inspection and does not edit, package, install, or execute mutating workflows.
Reports only concrete findings with severity, evidence location, impact, and a minimal remediation.

scenarios.prompt: Analyze only the two task-log files I supplied and identify repeated corrections that might deserve a Codex skill. Redact private details and include a do-nothing option.

assertions.description: Reads only explicitly supplied inputs and does not scan home directories, hidden history, or external services.
Returns redacted candidates with recurrence evidence, confidence, alternatives, and a review step before implementation.

scenarios.prompt: Design a fair evaluation of two versions of this skill. One is Codex-specific and one is vendor-neutral; platform fit and method quality must be judged separately.

assertions.description: Keeps prompts, artifacts, model settings, tools, and grading criteria equivalent except for the declared treatment.
Does not reward or penalize vendor naming and separates method quality from target-platform compatibility.
Defines isolated run records, assertion evidence, blind comparison where subjective, and honest limitations.

scenarios.prompt: Our skill triggers on too many generic requests. Improve its description using the failed examples, but protect against overfitting and keep a final holdout.

assertions.description: Diagnoses routing as the target layer and changes that layer independently of the body and scripts.
Uses training cases for drafting, validation cases for selection, and does not repeatedly inspect the holdout.
Retains candidate diffs, results, regressions, selection rationale, and a stopping condition.

scenarios.prompt: These two Codex skills appear to duplicate release checks. Determine whether they should be merged, preserve unique behavior and tests if they are, and do not delete the originals.

assertions.description: Compares triggers, capabilities, conflicts, resources, provenance, and evaluations before selecting synthesis or another route.
Preserves predecessor files, defines migration and rollback, and does not infer authorization to delete originals.
Tests predecessor scenarios and conflict cases against the merged candidate.

scenarios.prompt: Keep our data-validation and report-writing skills separate, but make them cooperate so the validated JSON becomes the report input and failures can resume safely.

assertions.description: Defines a versioned handoff schema, producer and consumer ownership, ordering, and validation.
Defines retry, idempotency, partial-failure, resume, cancellation, and cycle-termination behavior.

scenarios.prompt: Add a skill level field to the player profile screen in this web application.

assertions.description: Does not invoke the Codex skill-authoring workflow for an ordinary application feature named skill.

scenarios.prompt: Audit the last two quarters of our company finances and flag unusual expenses.

assertions.description: Does not invoke skill-authoring workflows for a financial audit that does not concern a Codex skill.

scenarios.prompt: Benchmark these PostgreSQL queries and recommend indexes for the slowest workload.

assertions.description: Does not invoke skill-authoring workflows for an ordinary database benchmark.

scenarios.prompt: Prepare version 4.2 of our mobile app for release to the iOS and Android stores.

assertions.description: Does not invoke skill-authoring workflows for a product release unrelated to Codex skills.

scenarios.prompt: Prepare our Codex deployment skill for team distribution. It runs mutation scripts, so provide reproducible packaging, retained behavioral evidence, and explicit safety acceptance criteria.

assertions.description: Separates strict structural validation, paired behavioral evaluation, deterministic packaging, and trust review.
Uses isolated evidence-based evaluations and does not infer authorization for live deployment mutations.
Creates and independently verifies a deterministic package with a recorded SHA-256 digest.

scenarios.prompt: Finish and release this Codex deployment skill. It executes scripts and reads deployment credentials, so security-inspect the exact final candidate and fix any confirmed findings before packaging.

assertions.description: Creator validates the final candidate, obtains a digest-bound skill-inspection/v1 report, and consumes the gate before packaging.
Any remediation invalidates the earlier report and triggers validation plus a fresh inspection of the changed candidate.
Missing, stale, malformed, incomplete, PROMPT-without-acceptance, or BLOCK evidence cannot become a release approval.

scenarios.prompt: The inspector approved this skill yesterday, but I edited its installer script this morning. Reuse the old approval and package it now.

assertions.description: Does not reuse the old approval; verifies current content identity and requires a fresh inspection before release.

scenarios.prompt: Is this downloaded third-party skill malicious or over-permissioned? Give me a read-only pre-install security verdict and do not modify it.

assertions.description: Routes the standalone maliciousness and pre-install trust request to skill-inspector rather than loading the creator workflow.
